_header: GRANDFATHERED: every uncoerced `+ (x || 0)` in tracked source as of
2026-09-11. Keyed on FILE + FIELD, never on a line number -- a term moving
down a file is not a new defect, and this repo has already been bitten by
a line-keyed exemption file that a one-line import silently invalidated.
THESE ARE NOT APPROVED, THEY ARE VISIBLE. `|| 0` does not make a value a
number: a non-empty string is TRUTHY, so the guard never fires and `+`
CONCATENATES. Measured: 0 + ("500" || 0) is the string "0500".
AND THE PLAUSIBLE CASE IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. A total of "abc" renders
"350abc" and somebody asks. A total of "500" renders "350500" -- a
believable $350,500 where the truth is $850 -- and nobody asks. In
SAIRNdental that figure was handed to Claude by vSpendAI() under a prompt
calling it "real, already-computed", so the fabrication would have
propagated into an AI answer as verified fact. That is the instance this
checker was built from.
A HAZARD, NOT A CONFIRMED DEFECT, and the distinction is the honest part.
The shape only bites where something can write a STRING to that field. A
field written only by app code that already does Number(x) || 0 cannot; a
field written through an API branch with no domain check can -- which is
exactly what dnt_vendor_orders was. The question each line asks is WHO CAN
WRITE THIS FIELD, and this tool cannot answer it.
TO BURN ONE DOWN: wrap the term in Number(...), which is the whole fix. Or,
if the field is provably numeric because everything that writes it coerces,
replace its line here with THAT REASON. Multiplication is safe and addition
term like s + (i.qty || 0) * (i.cost || 0) is listed for its `+` only.
WHAT THE FIRST RUN GOT WRONG, kept because it is the reason the tool strips
string interiors: stripping comments alone gave 193 occurrences. FIFTY-TWO
of those were the pattern quoted inside a STRING -- refusal messages and
documentation explaining this very defect, including this checker's own
subject in api/_lib/dental-ledger.js. More than a quarter of the first
result was the tool matching explanations of the bug rather than the bug.
